title: Degradation contracts and autoscaler holdback for controlled capacity drain
creator: Asha Kaur
description: Problem: During partial regional outages and load spikes we see autopilot autoscalers oscillate (scale down then back up) while downstream services are transitioning to degraded modes. That oscillation causes transient SLO violations for tail latency and error rate. Goal: introduce a system of 'degradation contracts' (per-route, per-tier agreements that describe acceptable degradation modes and percentages) combined with an 'autoscaler holdback' policy that prevents premature scale-down while graceful capacity-drain and fallback policies run. This task implements the API, controller changes, and telemetry needed to coordinate degradation policies with the autoscaler and rollout controllers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Define a minimal Degradation Contract schema that operators and product teams can declare per-route (yaml/Console) describing allowed degraded variants, max degraded QPS fraction, and drain windows.

2) Autoscaler holdback: when a Degradation Contract is active for a route, scale-down operations should be delayed for a configurable holdback window (default 120s) and use a staged drain plan instead of immediate eviction.
3) During staged drain, traffic is shifted according to the contract (e.g., 25% to degraded-variant A, 75% to primary) with no more than 10% increase in observed error rate in canary runs.

4) No new oscillation class failures introduced: measured using the existing autoscaler-thrash test; we must show a 40% reduction in scale-up/scale-down cycles during injected degradation compared to baseline.
5) Console surfaces: per-route "degradation state" and an autoscaler holdback flag; Grafana dashboard shows holdback counts, drain progress, and SLO impact.
6) Integration tests and load-test harness validated; runbook updated and on-call trained.
implementation_notes: Add DegradationContract CRD to controller-plane (fields: route, allowed_variants, max_degraded_fraction, drain_phases[], holdback_seconds)

Modify autoscaler controller to consult active DegradationContract before executing scale-down; if present, publish 'holdback' annotation on nodes/pools and schedule staged drain instead of immediate shrink.
Extend routing layer (smart-router) to support percentage-based split to degraded variants with atomic changepoints to prevent amplification loops.
Add TTL/expiry for temporary degradation contracts and an operator API to escalate or abort drains.
Telemetry: emit events 'degradation:entered', 'drain:phase_start', 'holdback:applied', and new metrics (holdback_count, drain_completion_seconds, degraded_qps_fraction).
Add backpressure hook: if degraded_variant has higher latency, automatically reduce degraded fraction by adaptive controller to avoid compounding SLO violations.
Charts: small Grafana dashboard for early testing; alert: 'drain_stalled' if drain_phase > configured_phase_timeout.
Testing: use existing chaos-sim infra to simulate regional failure and compare oscillation counts and SLO violations against baseline runs.
Docs: Confluence design + Console UI mockups linked below; update runbook with 'abort drain' and 'force scale-down' privileged actions.

decisions: Keep DegradationContract intentionally small - only fields necessary to run a safe staged drain; additional knobs postponed to follow-ups.
Default holdback_seconds=120 to balance SLO safety and capacity efficiency; make configurable per contract and via cluster-level policy.
Use percentage-based traffic splits for degraded variants rather than redirect-by-token; percentage splits integrate cleanly with routing calculus and autoscaler visibility.
Do not change autoscaler target utilization number; holdback prevents scale-down actions but the autoscaler still computes desired capacity for observability.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Degraded variants may amplify latency leading to worse SLOs. Mitigation: adaptive backpressure that reduces degraded fraction when tail latency crosses threshold and abort path to force primary scaling if possible.
Risk: Long holdback could waste capacity and increase cost. Mitigation: admin override and autoscaler policy to gradually reduce holdback if sustained cost pressure is detected (follow-up).

Risk: Interaction with multi-region failover controllers could create conflicting drains. Mitigation: add contract TTL and precedence rules: region-failover controllers set ephemeral override contracts with higher precedence.
Risk: Operator error when declaring contracts. Mitigation: Console validation + safe defaults and dry-run mode before enforcement.
